output:
**What I found:** All four behaviours you describe break standard access-control rules, so the tests must prove the opposite of each one. Under those tests the current model fails every row (the record calls this DEFER, because the architecture isn't fixed yet and the time limit for revoking invitations has no value).

**Why it matters:** As written, an editor can make themselves effectively an owner through an invite. A removed member's invitations still let people in. Two owners leaving at the same time can leave a workspace with no owner. A denied provisioning call leaves a disabled user row that can later block the real user. Tests written to match this description would lock all four defects in as intended behaviour.

**Do this first:**
1. Confirm with the product owner that the four behaviours are defects and not intent, and set the time limit for revoking invitations. The rows below assume they are defects.
2. Write the access decision as a pure function of grants and the request, so the property in row 5 can run without a database (`architecture-guidelines` access-control reference §3).

**What I did not check:**
- No code or existing tests were in scope, so this is a design from your description only. Close it by running an Audit-mode `test-strategy` pass on the access module once it exists.
- Whether disabled rows from past denied provisioning calls already exist in production. Check with a query for disabled users that have no successful provisioning event, then hand the cleanup to `evolutionary-database-design`.

| Risk / criterion | Failure mode | Oracle | Technique | Scope / fidelity | Dependencies | Data / environment | Evidence | Residual blind spot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 A grant can't exceed the grantor's own rights | An editor invites someone as owner (or anything above editor) | The invite is denied **and no invitation row is written** | Decision table: grantor role × invited role, every cell; plus a negative test on the store | Pure decision function for the table; one test against the real store that the write is absent | Real store for the negative test only | Seeded workspace with one member per role | None yet | Invites to another workspace: a decision for the Portfolio pass |
| R2 Invitations are re-checked when accepted | The grantor is removed or demoted after sending, and the invite still lets someone in, at the original role | Accepting is denied, or capped at the grantor's current role; no membership row is written | State transitions: send → demote or remove the grantor → accept | Component test, real store | Real store; the clock is controlled | Invitation fixture with its grantor | None yet | Undecided whether a demoted grantor's invite is downgraded or voided |
| R3 Revoking rights also revokes what came from them | A removed member's open invitations stay usable | Open invitations from that member are invalid within the time limit | State transitions plus a time-limit check | Component test, real store | Real store, controlled clock | — | DEFER: the time limit is unset | Sessions and tokens issued under the revoked rights |
| R4 A workspace always keeps an owner | The sole owner leaves; two owners leave or demote each other at once | The sole-owner leave is rejected and membership is unchanged. Under concurrency exactly one change succeeds and the owner count stays ≥ 1 | Negative example plus an interleaving test | Interleaving runs against the **real store**, because a fake can't show whether writes serialize | Real database; serialization owned by `concurrency-control` (a conditional write on the owner count or version) | Workspace with 2 owners, two transactions forced to interleave | None yet | Owner removed through IdP deprovisioning |
| R5 A denied request writes nothing | A denied provisioning call creates a disabled user row | No user row of any state appears; only an audit entry does. A later allowed call for the same identity succeeds | Negative test plus a follow-up example | Integration test at the provisioning endpoint with the real store; a contract test on the IdP payload | Real database; IdP request from the contract, not a free-form stub | Diff the users table before and after the call | None yet | Partial writes in other tables. The diff must cover every table the provisioning call writes |
| R6 Whole grant model | Any sequence of invite, accept, leave, demote, remove, provision reaches a state with a right nobody granted, or a workspace with no owner | Every right traces to a grant chain from an owner, and every workspace has ≥ 1 owner | Generative (property-based) / model-based testing | Pure decision function, no store | None | Generated actors, roles, sequences | None yet | Concurrency: covered by R4, not by this property |

```text
Subject:              Workspace access model (invite, accept, leave/demote, IdP provisioning)
Mode:                 Design
Strategy pass:        Obligation
Decision:             DEFER
Test basis:           User-stated model; architecture-guidelines access-control §1 rules (attenuation, re-check at acceptance, last owner, revocation, denial writes nothing)
Architecture basis:   not yet fixed
Quality risks:        1 privilege escalation via invite (R1, R6); 2 orphaned workspace (R4); 3 stale grant admission (R2, R3); 4 identity blocked by phantom disabled row (R5)
Manual evaluation:    none
Adequacy signals:     none — no portfolio exists; mutation testing on the decision function once written
Handoffs:             concurrency-control (R4 serialization); evolutionary-database-design (existing disabled rows); defect-shift-left (R6 at the stage that runs pure property tests, rows R2–R5 after Portfolio pass); requirements-traceability (R1–R6 IDs)
Residual risk:        R3 revocation bound unset; demoted-grantor invite semantics undecided; session/token revocation unscoped
Next action:          Owner confirms the four behaviours are defects and sets the revocation bound
Verification:         Not run — no code or tests in the working directory
```

Every negative test must check that the store is unchanged, not just that the request got a denied status. In R5, the current model returns a denial and still writes a row.
